newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RBA says gold sales have no effect on dividend.
newsitem.headline: RBA says gold sales have no effect on dividend.

text.p: A senior Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) official said its sale of 167 tonnes of gold over the last six months would not have an impact on the 1996/97 (July/June) dividend to be paid to the Australian government.

However, there may be an impact in future years of around A$100 million per year from the investment of the proceeds of the gold sales, RBA Assistant Governor, Financial Markets, Ric Battellino told Reuters.
"No, because the government has allowed the bank to keep all the proceeds," Battelino said when asked if the sales would impact on the 1996/97 RBA dividend to the government.
In the budget delivered in May, the government estimated it would receive a A$2.136 billion dividend from the RBA in 1996/97 and a A$1.200 billion dividend in 1997/98.
"There's no implication in the government for this at all," Battellino said. Changes in the amount of the RBA dividend could affect the government's budget forecasts.

"In the longer run, over time, the government will get extra dividends if we make more money by investing these proceeds. That might involve say an extra A$100 million a year on an ongoing basis," he said.
Asked later if the dividend was intact, Battellino replied : "Yes, it's certainly not affected by the gold (sales)."

The RBA said in a statement the gold sales had been undertaken forward and the first 125 tonnes had been delivered in June, with the remainder to be delivered in August and September. It will be left with gold reserves of 80 tonnes.
The proceeds of the sales were immediately invested in government securities denominated in U.S. dollars, Japanese yen and German marks, it said.
Treasurer Peter Costello confirmed Battellino's comments in a statement issued in Canberra.

"Before proceeding with the gold sales, the RBA sought, and received, my approval to re-invest the realised gains from the sale in other official reserve assets, rather than returning them as a dividend to consolidated revenue," he said.
"While such a dividend would have made a major boost to the Commonwealth budget, it would have been fiscally and prudentially irresponsible to have followed that course of action," he said.
"Such a dividend would have only been a one-off assistance to the budget in the year it was paid.

"Payment of such a dividend would have eroded the official reserve position of the RBA, and weakened its balance sheet which underpins Australia's financial system, and its standing in world markets," Costello said.
He said the gold sale proceeds will yield higher dividends to the government over the longer term.
